scenes.heading: Scale drawings
scenes.say: How does a map fit a whole city onto one page, while every street is still in the right place? The secret is scale. Let's learn how to read it and use it.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A 1 : 64 toy car: a 1 cm toy wheel is 64 cm on the real car
scenes.science: Scale 1 : n means every real length = drawing length × n
scenes.breaks: Toy makers fudge small details, but a true scale drawing shrinks every length exactly. Scales can enlarge too.
scenes.say: A toy car labelled one to sixty-four has every length shrunk by the same amount. A one centimetre toy wheel means a sixty-four centimetre real wheel. Same shape, just smaller.
scenes.caption: A toy car labelled 1 : 64 has every length shrunk by the same amount. A 1 cm toy wheel means a 64 cm real wheel. Same shape, just smaller.

scenes.heading: What a scale means
parts: length on the map or plan
length in real life, same unit
scenes.say: A scale is always drawing length to real length, in the same unit. In one to n, n is the scale factor. Drawing to real, multiply by n. Real to drawing, divide by n.

scenes.heading: Reading a map scale
scenes.say: Here's a map. First the two towns, then the dashed line between them, six centimetres long. The scale box says one to fifty thousand, so every centimetre on the map is fifty thousand centimetres in real life.
scenes.caption: The towns are 6 cm apart on the map. The scale is 1 : 50 000, so every 1 cm on the map is 50 000 cm in real life.

scenes.heading: Map to real life
scenes.question: Map scale 1 : 50 000. Towns are 6 cm apart on the map. Real distance in km?
scenes.say: On a one to fifty thousand map, two towns are six centimetres apart. Multiply: six times fifty thousand is three hundred thousand centimetres. A kilometre is one hundred thousand centimetres, so that's three kilometres.
scenes.caption: On a 1 : 50 000 map, two towns are 6 cm apart. 6 × 50 000 = 300 000 cm. 1 km = 100 000 cm, so that's 3 km.

scenes.heading: Finding the scale
scenes.question: A 6 cm drawing shows a car 2.4 m long. What is the scale?
scenes.say: A six centimetre drawing shows a car two point four metres long. First, same units: two hundred and forty centimetres. So drawing to real is six to two forty. Divide both by six, and the scale is one to forty.
scenes.caption: A 6 cm drawing shows a car 2.4 m long. Same units: 240 cm. Drawing : real is 6 : 240. Divide both by 6, and the scale is 1 : 40.

scenes.heading: Scale the lengths, then find the area
scenes.say: This garden is drawn twelve centimetres by eight, at one to five hundred. Scale each side first: sixty metres and forty metres. Then multiply to get two thousand four hundred square metres.
scenes.caption: The garden is drawn 12 cm by 8 cm at 1 : 500. Scale each side first: 60 m and 40 m. Then multiply: 2400 m².

scenes.heading: Watch out
points: Area: scale each length, then multiply
scenes.say: Watch out. Use the same units before you simplify. One kilometre is one hundred thousand centimetres, five zeros. If the first number is bigger, it's an enlargement. And for area, scale each length first, then multiply.
scenes.caption: Watch out. Use the same units before you simplify. 1 km = 100 000 cm, five zeros. If the first number is bigger, it's an enlargement. And for area, scale each length first, then multiply.

scenes.say: Quick recap. A scale is drawing to real, in the same units. Drawing to real, multiply. Real to drawing, divide. Then change your answer into sensible units. Now try the practice questions!
